title: Vibe-coded game file size
author: GlyndwrKog
selftext:
I've been building apps with AI, mostly using Flutter, and something I've noticed is that the final app sizes seem pretty large.  
For those with more traditional development experience, why is that? Is AI adding unnecessary code and dependencies, or is this just part of how mobile apps are built?  
More importantly, what do you guys do to keep your apps lean? Any particular habits, tools, or tricks that make a noticeable difference in the final APK/IPA size?

replies.author: GlyndwrKog
replies.body:
Yes but she only suggested I use WebP files for my assets instead of PNG. That only shaved about 10% of the file size. 

It’s not SUPER important to me, I am just curious why this happens… are LLM models giving us fluff and unnecessary methods and getters? Or is my app so complex that it’s actually a validly large file size? Ya know?

comments.author: 3tt07kjt
comments.body:
Flutter can be pretty large. I used Flutter a bit, years ago. In general, UI toolkits can be large, and Flutter has a UI toolkit in it.

If you want something smaller, you can go native. The smallest mobile apps use Java on Android or Objective C on iOS.

Kotlin / Swift are obvious improvements over Java / Objective C, but IIUC they both ship nontrivial runtimes in the app, rather than rely on runtimes which are shipped with the OS. You will see larger app sizes when you use them.

It’s a tradeoff. Reducing app size takes effort.

replies.author: GlyndwrKog
replies.body: Oh okay that’s good to know. I never considered the framework itself was a bulk of the size. Thanks!

replies.author: 3tt07kjt
replies.body: Yeah. Your actual code and assets is probably only a small percentage of the app. (Unless your app is big… I’m guessing it’s not.)

replies.author: GlyndwrKog
replies.body: My apps are 120-190mb but I feel like I see apps around the 60-90mb range mostly
